hook: The most people-pleasing thing you can do in a relationship is never tell someone what you actually need.
topic: How withholding needs is itself a form of relationship erosion
body:
**There's a version of people-pleasing that looks like generosity — but quietly hollows out the relationship.**

It's the version where you never say what you need. Where you manage your own disappointment so efficiently that no one ever has to know you were disappointed. Where you make everything easy and ask for nothing.

It feels kind. It feels selfless. It feels safe.

But here's what it actually does: it puts the other person in a relationship with a version of you that isn't fully real. They don't know what you need, so they can't meet it. They don't know where your edges are, so they can't respect them. And you spend years feeling vaguely unseen in a relationship you made deliberately opaque.

The most intimate thing you can do in a relationship isn't to ask less of people. It's to let them know what you actually need — and let them try.

Silence isn't safety. It's just a different kind of distance.

That's the full shift — link in bio.
